## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing: Conventional Memflation Accelerating; HBM Prices Now in YoY Decline**
TrendForce Q2 2026 (published June 1): conventional DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND Flash +70-75% QoQ — still blistering. Q1 actual came in +81% QoQ. HBM prices are now in year-over-year decline as competition among the three suppliers intensifies and buyer inventories build. TrendForce notes DDR5 profitability now rivals HBM3e — a structural shift. Conventional DRAM diverging bullishly from HBM pricing.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp: SK Hynix Slips to Q3; Micron Sold Out**
SK Hynix pushed HBM4 ramp from Q2 to Q3 2026. Micron early-ramped HBM4 and reports supply sold out through 2026. Samsung tracking ~50% HBM capacity expansion by year-end. The post-2026 pricing correction risk is not new, but HBM YoY price declines are arriving ahead of schedule, validating the baseline bear flag.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler Capex: No Fresh Prints; No Guide-Down**
No new capex guidance this week. Aggregate ~$700B+ unchanged. Google last raised to ~$190B; Amazon $200B; Meta $115-135B; Microsoft $110-120B. Zero guide-downs visible. Quiet on this signal.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASICs: No New Update**
AMD Helios on track for H2 2026 (last confirmed Feb 2026, no update this week). OpenAI's ~2 GW Trainium AWS commitment ramps from 2027, reinforcing ASIC share-shift thesis but not fresh news. Quiet.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics: CRDO Closes DustPhotonics Acquisition**
CRDO completed acquisition of DustPhotonics (silicon photonics) in May 2026, adding CPO-capable laser tech — expected to be a growth driver in FY2027. Coherent (COHR) demonstrated 1.6T transceivers at OFC 2026 across InP EML, SiPh, and VCSEL platforms — tech-neutral positioning for hyperscaler diversity. InP supply shortage intact through 2027.

**Signal 6 — Solar: Section 232 Tariff Threat Looms; FSLR 6th Plant on Track**
US module prices stable at ~$0.28/W but Section 232 tariffs on polysilicon could add $0.07-0.10/W and reignite upward pressure. FSLR sixth US manufacturing facility targeting H2 2026 — domestic-content story intact. No single-day catalyst on FSLR, ENPH, NXT, or ARRY today.

| **ALAB** | +203% (3 months) | Scorpio X-Series 320-Lane AI Fabric Switch launched May 2026, now shipping to cloud customers. Anthropic IPO filing (June 1) lifts AI-infra basket. |
| **CRDO** | Positive | DustPhotonics silicon photonics acquisition closes. Anthropic IPO filing seen as AI-infra demand catalyst for cable/interconnect suppliers. |
| **MU** | Recovering; ATH $1,089 → ~$996 | Q2 DRAM +58-63% QoQ is a direct earnings tailwind. Earnings due June 24. Wolfe Research PT raised to $1,250. Volatility from June 5 AVGO-triggered selloff fading. |
| **AVGO** | Triggered June 5 sector selloff; stabilizing | Beat Q2 but held (did not raise) long-term AI revenue outlook — flushed crowded longs. Q3 guide $29.4B (+89% YoY). Erste Group Buy upgrade June 5. Sector (NVDA -7%, MU -11.5%, MRVL -13%) has since partially recovered. |
| **HIVE** | Bullish targets | BUZZ subsidiary signed $30M in AI cloud contracts. FY2026 revenue +158% to $297.8M. 320 MW Toronto AI Gigafactory announced (CAD $3.5B; ops H2 2027). GPU cloud targeting $200M+ ARR by end of 2026. Dilution and crypto-correlation risks remain. |

No notable movers: NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU, COHR, LITE, CIEN, FSLR, ENPH, NXT, ARRY, WDC, STX, RMBS, SNDK, NVDA (stabilizing post-selloff).

---

## Context vs Baseline

HBM YoY price declines are arriving early — the SK Hynix "correction after 2026" warning is manifesting on pricing even while HBM volumes remain tight. Conventional DRAM is the offsetting bull: +81% actual in Q1, +58-63% guided for Q2. The MRVL catalyst is the textbook "must-catch" event: NVIDIA's CEO publicly naming a partner as a trillion-dollar candidate drove the stock 15-32% and triggered a wave of analyst upgrades. HIVE/BUZZ $30M cloud contract wins are directionally validating the AI/HPC pivot thesis, though scale remains small relative to BTC-mining revenue.

| Solar tariff risk | Section 232 threat rising | **Bear** near-term |
| MRVL (Jensen trillion-dollar call) | Sharp re-rating | **Bull** |

## Most Important Development

**MRVL: Jensen Huang publicly named Marvell "the next trillion-dollar company" at COMPUTEX.** The stock gained ~15-32% over the week. Q1 FY27 beat (+28% YoY, $2.42B rev), $2.7B Q2 guide, new Teralynx T100 switch chip, S&P 500 inclusion June 22, and a wave of analyst target raises to $200-250 make this the week's standout catalyst — and the exact "must-catch" scenario described in the watchlist instructions.
